lessons.title: Vectors
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Vectors, matrices, transformations (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Add, subtract and multiply column vectors by a number.
Find the magnitude of a vector, and the vector between two points.
Use position vectors, midpoints and parallel vectors.
reviewNotes: Column vector notation is written in plain text because the app's formula subset has no matrix environment (\binom is not supported): the notation (x, y) read downwards stands for the column vector. Check how the Cameroon Board writes vectors.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Column vectors
blocks.md: A vector has a size (magnitude) and a direction. We write its two components as (x, y): x is the horizontal move and y the vertical move (in print, the two numbers are stacked in a column). Add and subtract component by component; multiplying by k multiplies each component.

blocks.title: Magnitude and displacement
blocks.md: For $\vec{AB}$ with A and B having position vectors a and b, the vector from A to B, its magnitude, and the midpoint M of AB are:

blocks.title: Parallel vectors
blocks.md: Two vectors are **parallel** when one is a multiple of the other: (6, −4) = 2 × (3, −2). If $\vec{AB} = k\vec{CD}$ then AB and CD are parallel, and if the lines also share a point, A, B and C are collinear.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- $\vec{AB} = a - b$ is wrong: it is **b − a** (end minus start).
- $|\vec{AB}| = x + y$ is wrong: use Pythagoras.
- Reversing a vector changes its sign: $\vec{BA} = -\vec{AB}$.

blocks.title: Example 1: operations
blocks.statement: Given a = (3, −2) and b = (1, 4) (written as components), find 2a − b and |a|.

blocks.title: Example 2: between two points
blocks.statement: A has position vector (2, 3) and B has (6, −1). Find $\vec{AB}$, its magnitude and the midpoint M of AB.

lessons.title: Matrices (2 × 2)
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Vectors, matrices, transformations (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Find the determinant and inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix.
Solve simultaneous equations using the inverse matrix.
reviewNotes: Matrices are written in plain text '(a b / c d)' because pmatrix is not in the app's LaTeX subset; the figure of Example 1 shows a drawn matrix product. Check that the Cameroon O Level syllabus includes inverse matrices and simultaneous equations.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Matrices
blocks.md: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers. Here a 2 × 2 matrix (2 rows, 2 columns) is written row by row, rows separated by a slash: A = (a b / c d). Add and subtract corresponding entries. To **multiply**, combine each **row** of the first matrix with each **column** of the second: row × column.

blocks.title: Determinant and inverse
blocks.md: For A = (a b / c d) the determinant is below. If it is not 0, the inverse is (1/det) × (d −b / −c a): swap a and d, change the signs of b and c.

blocks.title: Useful facts
blocks.md: The identity matrix I = (1 0 / 0 1) leaves any matrix unchanged: AI = IA = A. A matrix with determinant 0 is **singular** and has no inverse. In general AB ≠ BA (order matters). $AA^{-1} = I$.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Multiplying entry by entry instead of row by column.
- Swapping the entries of the inverse incorrectly: swap a and d, **change the signs** of b and c.
- Forgetting to divide by the determinant.

blocks.title: Example 1: product and determinant
blocks.statement: A = (2 1 / 3 4) and B = (1 0 / 2 5). Find AB and the determinant of A.

blocks.title: Example 2: simultaneous equations
blocks.statement: Solve 2x + y = 7 and 3x + 4y = 18 with the inverse matrix.
steps: The matrix of coefficients is A = (2 1 / 3 4) with det 5, so $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{5}$ × (4 −1 / −3 2).

lessons.title: Transformations
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Vectors, matrices, transformations (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Reflect, rotate, translate and enlarge shapes on a coordinate grid.
Use scale factor for lengths and areas under enlargement.
reviewNotes: Transformation matrices are not included here: check whether the O Level syllabus asks for them (matrix of a transformation).
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: The four transformations
blocks.md:
- **Reflection**: in a mirror line (give the equation of the line).
- **Rotation**: give the centre, the angle and the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise).
- **Translation**: give the vector (x, y) of the movement.
- **Enlargement**: give the centre and the scale factor k.

blocks.title: Useful rules
blocks.md: Reflection in the y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y). In the x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y). In y = x: (x, y) → (y, x). Rotation of 90° anticlockwise about O: (x, y) → (−y, x). Under an enlargement of scale factor k the **lengths** are multiplied by k and the **areas** by k².

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Describing a rotation without the centre or direction (three details are needed).
- Enlargement: measuring distances from the shape instead of from the **centre**.
- A negative scale factor puts the image on the opposite side of the centre.

blocks.title: Example 1: reflection
blocks.statement: The triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 3). Find its image T' under reflection in the y-axis.
steps: Change the sign of every x-coordinate.

blocks.title: Example 2: describe a transformation
blocks.statement: Point P(2, 1) is moved to P'(−1, 2). Show that this is a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Then enlarge (2, 3) with centre (1, 1) and scale factor 3.
steps: Rule for 90° anticlockwise about O: (x, y) → (−y, x), so (2, 1) → (−1, 2). Matches P'.
Enlargement: vector from the centre to (2, 3) is (1, 2). Multiply by 3: (3, 6).
blocks.answer: **Rotation 90° anticlockwise about (0, 0); the image of (2, 3) is (4, 7).**
